prompts: We want to serve the model described in {WS}/MODEL.md on rented GPUs. Today's offers are in {WS}/offers.csv and our rental rules in {WS}/POLICY.md. Pick the cheapest way to serve it under the policy and justify the choice. Record it in {WS}/result.json with weights_gb, kv_cache_gb, total_gb, offer_id, usd_per_hour and usd_per_month.
answers:
[action] Wrote `result.json` with the chosen offer and memory figures.

[calc]
- Weights: 70B params × 1 byte (FP8) = 70 GB
- KV cache: 327,680 B/token × 32,768 tokens × 4 sequences = 42,949,672,960 B = 42.94967296 GB
- Runtime overhead: 8 GB
- Total needed: 120.94967296 GB usable VRAM (sharded across the offer's GPUs, so gpu_count × vram_gb_per_gpu must be ≥ ~120.95)

[filter] Offers meeting policy (in stock, region us-east/us-central/eu-west, ≤ US$4/h) with enough memory:
- of-117: 2×80 = 160 GB, $3.58/h — fits
- of-120: 1×141 = 141 GB, $3.79/h — fits
- of-124: 4×48 = 192 GB, $3.92/h — fits

Excluded: of-101/of-104/of-113 (96, 80, 96 GB — too small), of-108 (not in stock), of-129 ($4.89) and of-133 ($7.10) exceed the hourly cap, of-111 (ap-southeast) and of-137 (sa-east) wrong region.

[result] Cheapest compliant option: **of-117** (voltbay, us-central, 2× H100 80GB) at $3.58/h = 3.58 × 730 = $2,613.40/month. Assumptions: decimal GB throughout (as MODEL.md states), monthly = hourly × 730 per policy, no combining offers.

How I know it's right: the memory math is exact from MODEL.md's numbers (120.95 GB needed < 160 GB offered, > 96 GB of the next-largest fitting-and-legal-but-too-small options), and I checked every one of the 11 CSV rows against all four policy constraints; of the three survivors, of-117 has the lowest hourly price.
